fact: A standard NBA basketball game consists of 4 quarters of 12 minutes each, totaling 48 minutes of regulation play.
In basketball, a free throw is worth 1 point, a standard field goal is worth 2 points, and a shot made from beyond the three-point arc is worth 3 points.
Basketball was invented in December 1891 by Canadian physical education instructor Dr. James Naismith in Springfield, Massachusetts.
Michael Jordan led the Chicago Bulls to 6 NBA Championships in the 1990s (two three-peats: 1991-1993 and 1996-1998), winning Finals MVP on all 6 occasions.
LeBron James is the all-time leading scorer in NBA history, surpassing Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's longstanding record of 38,387 points in February 2023.
In the NBA, the shot clock gives the offensive team exactly 24 seconds to attempt a field goal that hits the rim.
Wilt Chamberlain holds the NBA record for the most points scored in a single game, scoring 100 points for the Philadelphia Warriors against the New York Knicks in March 1962.
Stephen Curry holds the all-time NBA record for the most career three-pointers made in regular season history, passing Ray Allen in 2021.
The standard height of a basketball rim above the court floor is exactly 10 feet (3.048 meters).
The Boston Celtics and Los Angeles Lakers are tied for the most NBA championships in history, each with 17 titles (prior to the Celtics' 18th title in 2024).
The Golden State Warriors set the NBA regular-season record with 73 wins and only 9 losses during the 2015-16 season.
In FIBA international basketball, games consist of 4 quarters of 10 minutes each, totaling 40 minutes of regulation play.
Klay Thompson holds the NBA record for the most three-pointers made in a single regular-season game, hitting 14 threes for Golden State against Chicago in 2018.
The 1992 USA Olympic Men's Basketball Team, known as the 'Dream Team', featured 11 future Hall of Fame players and defeated opponents by an average of 43.8 points.
Bill Russell won 11 NBA Championships in his 13 seasons with the Boston Celtics, the most championships won by any player in North American professional sports history.

Under NBA rules, a defensive three-second violation (illegal defense) occurs when a defender remains in the paint for more than 3 seconds without actively guarding an opponent, resulting in a technical free throw.
The highest-scoring game in NBA history took place on December 13, 1983, when the Detroit Pistons defeated the Denver Nuggets 186-184 in triple overtime (370 total points).
Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's trademark shot, the 'Skyhook', is widely considered the most unblockable scoring move in basketball history, contributing to his 6 MVP awards.
